claims.text: Use this guide to prepare questions before discussing an order.
SYNTHETIC ONLY: VMC-DEMO spindle rated 8000 rpm continuously under DEMO-SPINDLE-1 at 20 C; no cutting-load claim.
The synthetic spindle statement identifies a continuous rating and a named test method; its scope explicitly excludes a cutting-load claim.
A buyer enquiry should distinguish the stated spindle test conditions from the intended cutting application, then request evidence for any different duty or operating conditions.
Record the intended workpiece material, operating conditions and acceptance method in the enquiry so that the supplier can address applicability rather than relying on a headline rating.
Continue with the enquiry checklist and keep its limitations beside the corresponding statements.
SYNTHETIC ONLY: VMC-DEMO test piece tolerance +/-0.02 mm in aluminum at 20 C under DEMO-TEST-2 protocol; no other material or production guarantee.
The synthetic tolerance statement applies to an aluminum test piece under the stated method and temperature; it gives no guarantee for other materials or production conditions.
Request a representative test piece and an agreed measurement method for the intended material before treating the stated tolerance as a purchasing acceptance criterion.
SYNTHETIC ONLY: certificate DEMO-CNC-1 issued by Fictional Lab under DEMO-2026 for VMC-DEMO; expires 2027-01-01; no real certification.
The synthetic certificate identifies a fictional issuer, a named standard and a model scope; the statement explicitly says that it is not a real certification.
Ask for the original certificate, confirm the issuing body and covered model, and review its validity for the intended enquiry before making a certification statement to a buyer.
Keep the spindle test record, tolerance test record and certificate together with the enquiry; review each source against the intended use and retain any unresolved differences for clarification.
Prepare an enquiry and request the applicable evidence and limitations before proceeding.
